title: Rate Manual Note: How Age Moves the Base Monthly Premium on a Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Policy
content:
The base monthly premium a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is rated on moves with age according to the rating method the plan letter carries and the record of the policy itself.

| The policy record shows | What happens to the base monthly premium |
|---|---|
| The policy is rated on the age at issue and the age at issue is above 65 | It rises by the plan letter's issue-age step for each year of age above 65 |
| The policy is rated on attained age and the policy has been in force a full year or more | It rises by the plan letter's attained-age increase for each full year it has been in force |
| Neither of those holds | It is taken as it stands, whatever the policyholder's age |

### The two limbs of each row

Each of the first two rows requires both of its limbs. The first requires the rating method to be the age at issue and the age at issue to be above 65, so a policy rated on the age at issue whose policyholder was issued at exactly 65 has no year of age above 65 and falls to the last row. The second requires the rating method to be attained age and the policy to have been in force a full year or more, so an attained-age policy in force less than a full year falls to the last row.

The step in the first row is taken for each whole year of age above 65 at issue. The increase in the second row is taken for each full year the policy has been in force, part years counting for nothing.

### Hypothetical figures

A policy on Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan G, rated on the age at issue, issued at 68: the age at issue is 3 years above 65, and the base monthly premium of 164.20 rises by the plan letter's issue-age step of 2.8 per cent for each of those 3 years.

A policy on Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan A, rated on attained age, in force 30 months: that is 2 full years, and the base monthly premium of 112.40 rises by the plan letter's attained-age increase of 3.4 per cent for each of those 2 full years.

A policy rated on attained age and in force 7 months: the policy has not been in force a full year, so the base monthly premium is taken as it stands.
